title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 18
paragraphs: These Persians, having been sent to Amyntas, came into his presence and proceeded to demand earth and water for King Darius. He was willing to give both, and he also invited them to be his guests; he prepared a magnificent dinner and received the Persians with friendly hospitality. When dinner was over and the Persians were drinking pledges to one another, they said: “Macedonian host, it is the custom among us Persians, when we hold a great dinner, to bring in also our concubines and lawful wives to sit beside us. Since, therefore, you have received us so readily and are now entertaining us magnificently as your guests, and since you are willing to give King Darius earth and water, consent to follow our custom.” Amyntas replied: “Persians, among us the custom is not so, but that men should be separate from women. Since, however, you, being our masters, make this additional request, this too shall be granted you.” With these words Amyntas sent for the women; and when they came at his summons, they sat down in a row opposite the Persians. Then the Persians, seeing comely women, spoke to Amyntas and said that what had been done was very poorly arranged—it would have been better for the women not to come at all than to come and not sit beside them, but sit opposite and be a torment to their eyes. So Amyntas, under compulsion, bade the women sit beside the Persians; and when the women obeyed, the Persians, being far gone in drink, began at once to touch their breasts, and some of them no doubt also tried to kiss them.
